decisions.quote: Overall, the present research examines the correspondence between the TDM and SLM. This serves two replication purposes. It serves as a replication of earlier research (i.e., Murphy et al., 2011) that, with a somewhat small sample size, it showed a fair but no strong correspondence between these two measures; and it helps us to explore whether the associations with attachment, number of siblings, and age are similar for the two measures.
decisions.reason: Prior adjudication and state files at the supplied context paths do not exist (never-adjudicated work). In addition to replicating Van Lange, De Bruin, Otten, & Joireman (1997, 10.1037/0022-3514.73.4.733, matched to shipped row input_row_index 1605 / blind target_index 0), the paper sets out as Goal 1 to empirically replicate Murphy, Ackermann, & Handgraaf's (2011) finding on the correspondence between the Triple Dominance Measure (TDM) and the Slider Measure (SLM) of social value orientation ('Overall, the present research examines the correspondence between the TDM and SLM. This serves two replication purposes. It serves as a replication of earlier research (i.e., Murphy et al., 2011) that, with a somewhat small sample size, it showed a fair but no strong correspondence between these two measures'). In the Results section ('Correspondence between TDM and SLM', pp. 407-408) and Discussion ('Association between TDM and SLM', p. 410), the authors test the classification agreement and shared variance between the TDM and SLM across two new samples (N = 1,446 and N = 2,644), finding 75% same-category agreement (Cohen's kappa = .61 excluding unclassified participants, .52 including unclassified, ps < .001) and concluding that this medium-sized correspondence is consistent with Murphy et al. (2011). The reference list (p. 416) and Crossref metadata verify the identity of Murphy, R. O., Ackermann, K. A., & Handgraaf, M. J. J. (2011), 'Measuring social value orientation', Judgment and Decision Making, 6(8), 771-781, DOI 10.2139/ssrn.1804189. Because the sole shipped row (input_row_index 1605) is Van Lange et al. (1997), an independent study by different authors published 14 years earlier before the SLM existed, report equivalence does not apply and Murphy et al. (2011) is a genuinely missing original target.
